dataset: Mission Architect In-Game Educational Guide & 30s Demo Storyboard

explanations.shortExplanation: Higher orbits travel slower over a longer circle, so each lap takes much longer: ~92 minutes at 400 km LEO versus 23 h 56 m at 35,786 km GEO.
explanations.tradeOffTip: Pick LEO/SSO for frequent passes over wildfires, or GEO if you want to match Earth's spin and stare at one continent permanently.
explanations.sourceLabel: NASA Earth Observatory — Catalog of Orbits

explanations.shortExplanation: Whenever Earth or the Moon blocks the Sun, solar panels drop to 0 W and your battery must power the entire spacecraft until sunrise.
explanations.tradeOffTip: A 40 Wh battery survives short low-power orbits, whereas power-hungry X-band radios or 69-minute GEO equinox shadows require the 120 Wh pack.
explanations.sourceLabel: NASA Ames SmallSat SOA — Power & Energy Storage

explanations.shortExplanation: The smallest feature your camera can distinguish on the ground equals your orbit altitude multiplied by the sensor's angular resolution.
explanations.tradeOffTip: Moving 50x higher to GEO makes a standard LEO camera 50x blurrier (~27 km pixels)—you need the Wide-Field GEO Telescope to keep pixels under 1 km.
explanations.sourceLabel: NASA FIRMS — Spatial Resolution of MODIS vs VIIRS

explanations.shortExplanation: Cameras continuously write GB of imagery to onboard flash memory, which can only empty while flying within line-of-sight of a NASA ground station.
explanations.tradeOffTip: If your camera creates 24–32 GB/day and an S-band antenna only sends 12 GB/day, memory hits 100% and new wildfire alerts are dropped—upgrade to X-band!
explanations.sourceLabel: NASA SCaN — Near Space Network Ground Stations

explanations.shortExplanation: Reaching Geostationary or Lunar orbit takes far more rocket delta-v than LEO, drastically shrinking how much mass a launcher can lift—or blocking small rockets altogether.
explanations.tradeOffTip: Lighter buses let you ride Small ($8M) or Rideshare ($6M/100kg) rockets in LEO/SSO, freeing budget for better sensors.

explanations.shortExplanation: Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) and Solar Energetic Particles (SEPs) increase radiation upsets and heat Earth's upper atmosphere, raising drag in LEO.
explanations.tradeOffTip: Radiation-hardened computers and medium bus shielding reduce failure risk during intense storms like the May 2024 Gannon G5 event.
explanations.sourceLabel: NASA CCMC DONKI Space Weather Database
